headline: U.S. scraps crypto wallet reporting rule as Zcash jumps 3.3% on $100M mining commitment
summary: The U.S. government withdrew a proposed rule that would have required reporting of crypto transfers over $10,000 to private wallets — a meaningful win for self-custody advocates and privacy-focused assets. Zcash led the top-15 gainers on a separate catalyst: Fortitude committed up to $100 million in mining equipment to expand ZEC operations. The broader market barely moved, with Bitcoin and Ethereum each within a fraction of a percent of yesterday's close, but the regulatory news and a pair of product announcements gave the day more substance than the price action suggests.

winners.name: OKB
winners.catalyst: OKX launched 'OKX Money,' a new app feature allowing users to save, earn 10% yield, and spend dollar stablecoins in one platform, boosting sentiment around the OKX ecosystem token. The product announcement drove speculative buying in OKB as traders priced in increased platform utility and user growth.

losers.name: Ethena
losers.catalyst: No specific catalyst was identified for Ethena's decline; the drop likely reflects broader altcoin rotation or profit-taking in the DeFi sector, as mid-cap DeFi tokens lagged while smaller-cap assets outperformed.

whyItMoved:
The headline story today was regulatory, not price action. The U.S. government withdrew a proposed rule that would have required anyone sending more than $10,000 in crypto to a private wallet (one you control yourself, not held by an exchange) to file a report with authorities. Separately, FinCEN also dropped a proposed rule targeting crypto mixing services, citing concerns about a chilling effect on legitimate activity. Together, these withdrawals represent a meaningful shift in tone from U.S. regulators — less surveillance pressure on ordinary users and privacy-preserving tools.

Zcash was the clearest beneficiary in the top 15, rising 3.30% to $1,369.82. The direct catalyst was Fortitude's commitment of up to $100 million in mining equipment to expand ZEC operations — a concrete, fundamental demand signal. Monero, another privacy-focused asset, gained 1.96%, likely catching a tailwind from the same regulatory news, as both assets had faced the prospect of heightened scrutiny under the now-withdrawn rules.

OKB's 5.69% gain — the day's biggest move across all tracked assets — traced directly to OKX's launch of 'OKX Money,' an integrated product letting users save at 10% yield and spend dollar stablecoins from a single app. Exchange ecosystem tokens tend to respond to product announcements like this because expanded platform utility can drive user growth and token demand.

Bitcoin and Ethereum barely registered a move — up 0.14% and down 0.07% respectively. The Fear & Greed index sits at 73, in Greed territory, suggesting the market is broadly comfortable but not euphoric. The day's story was in the regulatory and product news, not the price tape.
worthKnowing: Ethereum's Glamsterdam testnet received a last-minute bug fix ahead of a major network upgrade expected to significantly increase chain capacity, keeping the upgrade timeline on track.

The Treasury's withdrawal of the crypto mixing rule — dropped alongside the self-hosted wallet reporting proposal — marks a broader regulatory pullback that removes two proposed compliance burdens from the industry simultaneously.
OKX Money offers 10% yield on dollar stablecoins held within the app, expanding OKX's footprint into consumer finance alongside its existing exchange business.
